name: Commit Message Quality
description: Write descriptive commit messages that explain why a change was made, not just what changed.
content:
# Commit Message Quality Rules

- Write commit messages that explain WHY the change was made — the diff already shows WHAT changed
- Use a conventional prefix — `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `chore:`, `perf:`, `ci:`
- Keep the subject line under 72 characters — wrap the body at 72 characters
- Use imperative mood in the subject — "Add user validation" not "Added user validation" or "Adds user validation"
- Separate subject from body with a blank line — the subject is for quick scanning, the body is for details
- Reference issue numbers when applicable — `fix: prevent crash on empty input (fixes #42)`
- Don't use generic messages — "fix bug", "update code", "WIP", "misc changes" are useless to future readers
- Each commit should represent one logical change — don't mix a feature addition with an unrelated refactor
- If a commit reverts a previous change, explain why — `revert: undo user cache (caused memory leak in #78)`
- Don't commit generated files, build artifacts, or temporary debugging code
- Squash fixup commits before merging — the main branch history should be clean and meaningful
- Include relevant context in the body — what alternatives were considered, what tradeoffs were made
